phase16_findings.title: Mobile layout unusable: fixed 220px sidebar leaves 155px for content, tables and cards overflow off-screen
phase16_findings.expected: At mobile widths, the sidebar should collapse (hamburger / stacked nav) and content should fit the 375px viewport without horizontal scrolling to read data.
phase16_findings.actual: At 375px the sidebar still occupies a fixed 220px (59% of the viewport), leaving a 155px-wide scrolling strip for all content. On #users, the users table renders 448px wide starting at x=264, running to x=712 — ~337px of the table is unreachable off the right edge. On #dashboard, the 4 stat cards each render 200px wide in the 155px column, overflowing. Nav link tap targets overlap partially off-screen (Sign In at x=479). The layout never collapses: no hamburger, no stacked nav, no responsive breakpoints.
phase16_findings.impact: Mobile users cannot read any data — user emails, plan, status and join dates are cut off, and the dashboard stat cards bleed off-screen. The app is effectively desktop-only despite being a live web app.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add responsive CSS: below ~768px collapse the fixed sidebar into a top bar with a hamburger toggle (or stack nav links), let the main content span full width, and make the users table horizontally scr

phase16_findings.title: Sign In link leads to #login but no login form is ever rendered — authentication is unreachable
phase16_findings.expected: A login form (email/username + password + submit) should render so users can authenticate.
phase16_findings.actual: The URL changes to http://localhost:9904/#login but the content area renders nothing: no form, no username/password fields, no Sign In button. The page title remains stale ('Workspace Settings' from the previous view) and the main area is empty below the header.
phase16_findings.impact: Users cannot sign in at all. The entire user_login workflow (navigate, enter credentials, submit, verify authenticated) is impossible, and any authenticated features behind it are unreachable.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Implement the login view for the '#login' route (or point the Sign In link at an existing route). Also add a router fallback so unmapped hashes show a 'not found' message instead of a blank page.

phase16_findings.title: Dashboard chart is a placeholder — no actual chart is rendered anywhere in the app
phase16_findings.expected: A 'Revenue Trend (Last 30 Days)' chart should render actual data (lines/bars) as the card title promises.
phase16_findings.actual: The only chart in the app is a grey box containing the literal text '📈 Chart visualization area'. There is no line, bar, or any other visualization, and no canvas/svg elements. Hovering does nothing.
phase16_findings.impact: The core 'view metrics/charts' workflow is not implemented. Users cannot see any trend data, which is the primary purpose of an analytics dashboard.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Implement an actual chart (e.g. a simple SVG/canvas line chart of the last 30 days) or remove the card until data visualization is available.

phase16_findings.title: Invite User form accepts invalid email with no validation or any success/failure feedback
phase16_findings.expected: The form should validate the email address, show an error message such as 'Please enter a valid email', or if accepted, show a confirmation that the invite was sent.",
phase16_findings.actual: The modal closes immediately with no validation error, no toast, no success message, and no new row in the users table. The user has no way to know whether the invite was sent or silently discarded. An empty-email submit likewise shows no error.
phase16_findings.impact: Admins cannot tell whether an invitation was actually sent. Invalid addresses are accepted without complaint, so typos silently produce dead invites.",
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add email format validation (e.g. input type=email + pattern or a JS check) that shows an inline error and keeps the modal open, and show a success toast/confirmation on a valid submit.",

phase16_findings.title: Unknown hash routes render a blank page with a stale title instead of a 404/fallback view
phase16_findings.expected: An unknown route should show a '404 / page not found' message or fall back to the default dashboard view.
phase16_findings.actual: Navigating to an unmapped hash such as #nonexistent leaves the content area blank while keeping the previous view's stale title, with no console error and no 'page not found' message.
phase16_findings.impact: Users who mistype or follow a broken deep link see a dead blank page with a misleading title, with no way to know what happened.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add a router catch-all: for unmatched hashes, either render a friendly not-found view or redirect to #dashboard.

phase16_findings.title: 'No API keys configured.' message stays visible after an API key is generated
phase16_findings.expected: The empty-state message should be hidden once a key exists, replaced by the key display.
phase16_findings.actual: After clicking Generate API Key, a key (e.g. 'mk_f712xuzzna') appears in #api-key-display, but the paragraph 'No API keys configured.' (#settings-view > div:nth-of-type(2) > p) remains visible directly above it.
phase16_findings.impact: Contradictory UI ('No API keys configured' next to a configured key) confuses users about the actual state of their workspace.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Toggle the empty-state paragraph's visibility when a key is generated (hide it when the key list is non-empty).

phase16_findings.title: Dashboard MRR ($28,450) disagrees with Revenue page Total MRR ($28,441)
phase16_findings.expected: Both views should report the same MRR figure for the same period.
phase16_findings.actual: Dashboard shows Revenue (MRR) of $28,450 while the Revenue page shows Total MRR of $28,441. The Revenue page's total is arithmetically consistent with its own rows (Basic 890×$9.99=$8,891; Pro 357×$49.99=$17,846; Enterprise 3×$568=$1,704; sum $28,441), so the dashboard figure is the outlier by $9.
phase16_findings.impact: Users comparing the dashboard KPI to the revenue breakdown see two different numbers for the same metric, undermining trust in the analytics.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Derive the dashboard MRR stat from the same data source/computation as the Revenue breakdown table rather than hardcoding separate values.

phase16_findings.title: All signup CTAs are non-functional — no registration flow exists
phase16_findings.expected: Clicking Get Started Free or a pricing plan button should start a signup/checkout flow — a registration form at minimum.
phase16_findings.actual: Nothing happens. No navigation, no modal, no signup form. The nav button (#cta-btn) and hero anchor (#hero-start) both have placeholder hrefs/targets and no handler. GET /signup returns 200 but serves the marketing landing page, not a registration screen.
phase16_findings.impact: The entire signup_flow workflow (click_cta, fill_registration, submit_form, access_account) is impossible. New users cannot register, making the product's core funnel — and its revenue path via the three paid plans — completely non-functional.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Wire the CTAs to a real signup route. Build a registration form (email/password/plan) and route plan buttons into it with the selected plan pre-filled.

phase16_findings.title: Sign In link is dead — no login page or form exists anywhere
phase16_findings.expected: Clicking Sign In should take the user to a login page or open a sign-in form where credentials can be entered.
phase16_findings.actual: Nothing happens. The URL stays at http://localhost:9905/, no modal or form appears, no network request is fired (browser_diagnostics shows no new requests), and no console error is raised. The element renders as an anchor with href="#" and no JS handler. Directly navigating to /login also fails: the server responds 200 but serves the identical marketing landing page rather than any login screen, so no way exists to authenticate.
phase16_findings.impact: Returning users cannot sign in at all. The entire user_login workflow (navigate_to_login, enter_credentials, submit_login, verify_authenticated) is unreachable, blocking access to any authenticated area of the product.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Implement a login route (or modal) and point #signin-link at it with a real href. The current href="#" is a placeholder that was never wired up.

phase16_findings.title: No mobile responsiveness: page renders as fixed 768px layout scaled to unreadable size on phones
phase16_findings.expected: Below ~768px the layout should collapse to a single column, the nav should stack or become a hamburger menu, and text should remain readable (16px+) with touch targets of at least 44×44px.
phase16_findings.actual: The page has no responsive behavior below 768px. At 375×812 every element keeps its tablet coordinates (header 768px wide, Sign In link at x=602, Get Started button at x=644 — all beyond the 375px viewport edge), and the browser shrink-to-fits the whole 768px layout into the phone screen. Body text renders at roughly 8-9px effective size and hero H1 at ~14px; navigation links become tap targets around 32×18px. No hamburger menu, no stacking, no breakpoint exists between 375px and 768px.
phase16_findings.impact: On any phone the site is effectively unusable: marketing copy is too small to read and nav links/CTAs are far below minimum tap-target size. Mobile visitors — typically the majority of marketing-site traffic — bounce, compounding the already-broken conversion funnel.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add a mobile breakpoint (max-width ~768px or ~640px): stack feature/pricing cards vertically, collapse the nav into a hamburger or logo-only bar with the CTAs, and drop fixed pixel widths/min-widths o

phase16_findings.title: Testimonials and About nav links point to sections that don't exist; page has no footer
phase16_findings.expected: The Testimonials and About navigation links should scroll to sections containing testimonials and about/company content, respectively. A marketing page of this type would normally also have a footer.
phase16_findings.actual: Both links update the URL hash but land the user on the pricing section, because no element with id="testimonials" or id="about" exists in the DOM. The page ends at the Enterprise pricing card. There is also no footer of any kind.
phase16_findings.impact: Two of the four main navigation links are broken. Users clicking them see the pricing section instead of the promised content, which reads as a broken or unfinished site.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add the missing <section id="testimonials"> and <section id="about"> elements with content, plus a standard footer. Alternatively, remove the two nav links until content exists.

phase16_findings.title: Leads do not persist — all created/advanced leads are lost on page reload (contacts do persist)
phase16_findings.expected: All user-entered CRM data should persist across page reloads; leads and contacts should behave identically.
phase16_findings.actual: Contacts persist across a full page reload, but leads silently vanish. After creating 'QA Automation Lead' ($5,000, Website) and advancing it to Won, a reload of #leads showed only the 3 seeded leads — the created lead and its stage progression were gone. In the same session, a contact created via the Add Contact modal ('QA Persist Test') DID survive an identical reload.
phase16_findings.impact: A sales rep who logs a lead and advances it through the pipeline loses all of that work the moment the page is refreshed or the browser is reopened. Pipeline tracking — a core requirement — is effectively unusable for real work, and the inconsistency (contacts save, leads don't) makes data loss unpredictable.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Leads are likely held in a plain in-memory array while contacts use localStorage. Route leads through the same persistence layer (localStorage or backend API) as contacts, and re-render on load.

phase16_findings.title: Created data is lost on page reload — no persistence layer (contacts, and likely all entities)
phase16_findings.expected: The newly created contact should still be present after a page reload, since saving implies durable storage (backend or localStorage).
phase16_findings.actual: After reload the table shows only the two seed contacts (John Smith, Jane Doe). The 'QA Test User' record is gone. All data is held in a JavaScript in-memory array and re-seeded on every load. No network requests are issued on save (browser_diagnostics shows no POST/PUT), confirming nothing is sent to a server.
phase16_findings.impact: Any contact, lead, or deal a sales rep enters is destroyed by a refresh or by closing the tab. For a CRM whose whole purpose is storing customer data, this makes the app unusable as a real tool and risks silent loss of all entered data.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Persist state: either back the app with a real API/database, or at minimum serialize the state array to localStorage and rehydrate on load instead of re-seeding hard-coded demo rows.

phase16_findings.title: Sign In link leads to a completely blank page — login is unusable
phase16_findings.expected: A login form with email/password fields (or equivalent) should render, allowing the user to authenticate.
phase16_findings.actual: The #login route renders only the top navigation bar. The entire content area is blank — no form, no inputs, no text. The URL changes to /#login but nothing appears. No console errors are thrown, so the route handler simply shows no content.
phase16_findings.impact: Users cannot sign in at all. The build prompt calls for a CRM for a sales team, which implies multi-user authentication; the entire authentication flow is dead. Combined with the fact that all other pages are reachable without signing in, there is no way to establish an authenticated session.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Implement the #login route view: a form with email and password inputs and a submit handler. Check the router config — the login section appears to be referenced in the nav but no matching section/tem

phase16_findings.title: Pipeline page shows empty columns — no deals rendered in any stage, drag-and-drop unimplemented
phase16_findings.expected: Each pipeline column should display the leads/deals currently in that stage, with the ability to move them between stages.
phase16_findings.actual: All four columns render as empty headers with no cards. The page itself admits 'Drag and drop deals between stages (coming soon).' Even after creating a new lead, no card appears in any column.
phase16_findings.impact: The build prompt explicitly demands pipeline tracking ('leads, pipeline'), and the expected 'lead to deal' workflow ends here. Sales teams cannot see or manage their pipeline at all; the feature is a visual placeholder.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Render each lead as a card in its stage column, and implement the stage-change interaction (drag-and-drop or buttons). The lead stage advancement on #leads suggests the data model already supports it.

phase16_findings.title: Contacts cannot be edited or viewed — no detail page, no edit action
phase16_findings.expected: A CRM should allow opening a contact record to view details (phone, notes, history) and editing fields like name, email, company and status.
phase16_findings.actual: The Actions column contains only a 'Delete' button. Contact names are plain text, not links. There is no edit form, no detail view, and no way to change a contact's status (e.g. 'New' → 'Active'). The only two operations available are create and delete.
phase16_findings.impact: The expected 'contact lifecycle' workflow (create, view, edit, delete) is only 50% implemented. Sales reps cannot correct a typo, update a company, or change contact status — they must delete and re-enter the record.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add an Edit action per row that opens the same form pre-filled, and a contact detail view. Also allow status changes from the list.

phase16_findings.title: Dashboard stats are hard-coded and never reflect actual data (Total Leads stuck at 5)
phase16_findings.expected: Dashboard KPIs should be computed from the current leads data and update when leads are created, advanced, or deleted.
phase16_findings.actual: The stat tiles are static: 'Total Leads: 5', 'Won Deals: 1', 'Pipeline Value: $45,000' at all times. After creating a 4th lead (QA Automation Lead, $5,000), the dashboard still showed 5/1/$45,000 — unchanged before and after. The Leads table itself contained only 3 rows at page load (Acme Corp Lead, TechSoft Demo, Global Inc), so even the initial '5' is wrong.
phase16_findings.impact: The dashboard — the first screen a sales manager sees — reports numbers that do not reflect reality. Decisions made on stale/wrong KPIs are a core CRM failure. Also no 'Total Contacts' KPI exists despite contacts being a headline feature.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Derive the tiles from the same leads array that feeds the Leads table, and recompute on every data mutation. Add a Total Contacts tile sourced from contacts.length.

phase16_findings.title: Delete contact has no confirmation dialog — single click irreversibly removes data
phase16_findings.expected: A confirmation prompt ('Are you sure you want to delete John Smith?') before permanent removal.
phase16_findings.actual: The row disappears immediately on click, with no confirm(), no modal, and no undo option. A stray click on the wrong row destroys the record with no recovery.
phase16_findings.impact: Accidental data loss from a single mis-click, with no undo. In a sales context, deleting a customer record by accident and having no way to recover it is a real data-integrity problem.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add a confirmation dialog or an undo toast. At minimum require a second explicit confirmation click.

phase16_findings.title: Contact form accepts invalid email and empty/blank values without validation
phase16_findings.expected: Email field should be validated for format (e.g. user@domain.tld) with an inline error; empty Company may be acceptable but should be a conscious choice.
phase16_findings.actual: The record saves successfully with email 'notanemail' and an empty company. Only the presence of Name and Email is checked ('Name and email required'); no format validation of any kind runs.
phase16_findings.impact: Contacts with invalid emails pollute the database and make email-based features (export, mail-merge, dedupe) unreliable. Whitespace-only names are also likely accepted since only truthiness appears to be checked.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add a regex or browser-native email input type=email with a pattern check on the email field, and trim inputs before the required check.

phase16_findings.title: Navigation is broken: Team, My Tasks, Reports and Sign In links never change the view
phase16_findings.expected: Clicking "My Tasks" should show a personal task list, "Team" should show the team/member page, "Reports" should show reports, and "Sign In" should show a login form.
phase16_findings.actual: Clicking each link changes the URL hash (e.g. to http://localhost:9902/#team, #reports, #login) but the visible page remains the "Project Board" kanban view. No view element for Team, Tasks, Reports, or Login is ever present in the DOM (verified with waitFor on selectors #team-view, #tasks-view, #reports-view, #login-view — none exist). Reloading the page directly at #reports still renders the Board.
phase16_findings.impact: Four of the five sections advertised in the app's own navigation are unreachable, including the Sign In entry point required for the CRITICAL login workflow. Team management, My Tasks, and Reports are effectively missing functionality, not just broken links.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Implement the view-switching logic (e.g. a hashchange listener that shows/hides #team-view, #tasks-view, #reports-view, #login-view) or remove the dead links. The views' DOM containers appear to be ab

phase16_findings.title: Kanban "Done" column is clipped off-screen at tablet width with no way to scroll to it
phase16_findings.expected: The kanban board should either fit the viewport or scroll horizontally so all four columns (To Do, In Progress, Review, Done) are reachable at tablet width.
phase16_findings.actual: At 768×1024 the four kanban columns (each 250px + gap) total ~1044px but the #kanban container is only 720px wide and does not scroll horizontally. The "👁 Review" column is partially clipped and the "✅ Done (2)" column is completely off-screen. Scrolling the page (deltaX=300) and scrolling directly on the #kanban element both fail to reveal it. The body as a whole does not overflow horizontally at this width (body width stays 768, nav stays at x=0).
phase16_findings.impact: Tablet users cannot see or interact with the Done column (and can only partially see Review), so completed tasks are invisible and any task advanced to Done disappears from view for them.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add overflow-x: auto (with a snap or min-width) to the #kanban container, or switch to a responsive column layout (2×2 grid / vertical stacking with column selectors) below ~900px.

phase16_findings.title: New Task form gives no validation feedback when Title is empty or whitespace-only
phase16_findings.expected: The form should show a visible validation error (e.g. "Title is required") and/or mark the Title field invalid so the user understands why nothing happened.
phase16_findings.actual: Clicking "Create" with an empty Title (and separately with a Title of four spaces) does nothing: no task is created, no error message appears, no field is highlighted, and the modal stays open. The only feedback is the absence of a new card.
phase16_findings.impact: Users who submit without a title get silent failure; they may believe the app is broken. Whitespace-only titles are also indistinguishable from a bug since there is no messaging at all.
phase16_findings.recommendation: Add explicit client-side validation: show an inline error under the Title field and/or set the input's required attribute + aria-invalid so the browser and assistive tech communicate the problem. Trim

phase16_findings.title: Mobile header navigation overflows the viewport; "Sign In" link is off-screen
phase16_findings.expected: The header navigation should fit the mobile viewport (single-line links, wrapping to a second row or a hamburger menu) with no horizontal page overflow and readable labels.
phase16_findings.actual: At 375×812 the header nav links wrap to two cramped lines: "📋 TaskBoard" (42px tall), and the links "My Tasks" (37.5×32) and "Sign In" (30.5×32) render as two-line wrapped text. "Sign In" sits at x=398–429, entirely outside the 375px viewport until the user scrolls the page horizontally.
phase16_findings.impact: On phones the "Sign In" link is off-screen and "My Tasks" is illegibly wrapped ("My / Tasks"), plus the whole page scrolls sideways. Mobile users cannot reach Sign In without sideways scrolling.
